title: Braised Beef Short Ribs
subtitle: Slow-braised beef ribs in red wine and aromatics
excerpt: Beef short ribs braised for three to four hours in red wine and stock with aromatics until the meat has pulled away from the bone and sits in a glossy, intensely reduced sauce. A long cook; the result is transformatively good.

recipe.sourceNotes: Braised beef short ribs entered fine dining menus in the early 2000s as chefs rediscovered the potential of long-cooked secondary cuts. Short ribs (the thick meaty ribs from the chuck end of the rib cage) have dense connective tissue and intermuscular fat that respond beautifully to the moist heat of a long braise, becoming extraordinarily tender and yielding a rich, gelatinous sauce from the dissolved collagen. They are related to the Korean galbi (which uses the same cut marinated and grilled) and appear in various forms across American barbecue, French pot-au-feu, and British cooking. The wine braise is the dominant restaurant preparation: four short ribs, one bottle of wine, a full day's work, and the most impressive dinner party main course available.

content.text: Brown the short ribs very thoroughly on all sides; this step cannot be rushed. The Maillard crust that forms is the primary flavour base for the braise. The ribs should cook in the oven, not on the hob; the gentler, even heat of the oven produces more consistent results. Make this the day before and chill: the fat solidifies on top and can be lifted off, leaving a cleaner, more concentrated sauce.

items.preparation: bone-in beef short ribs; 4 large pieces or 8 smaller ones

content.text: Season the short ribs. Heat the oil in a large ovenproof casserole over the highest heat. Brown the ribs in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deeply coloured on all surfaces. Remove.

Cook the vegetables and garlic in the remaining fat until softened. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and reduce by half. Add the stock, bay, and thyme. Return the ribs, ensuring they are mostly submerged.

Cover and cook in the oven at 150°C / fan 130°C / gas 2 for 3 to 3.5 hours until the meat is pulling away from the bone. Remove the ribs carefully. Strain the sauce into a clean pan, pressing the vegetables. Reduce over high heat until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Return the ribs. Serve over mashed potato or polenta.
